[Image: Coordinate grid with points M and N]

Two points M and N are shown in the figure above. John is looking for a point P such that MNP is an isosceles triangle. Which of these points could be point P?
figure_description: A 6-by-6 grid in the first quadrant of a Cartesian coordinate system. The horizontal x-axis has an arrow pointing to the right, labeled x, with origin O and tick marks labeled 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. The vertical y-axis has an arrow pointing upwards, labeled y, with tick marks labeled 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. Grid lines are drawn at each integer value from 1 to 6. Two points are plotted on the grid: point M at (1, 2), labeled M, and point N at (5, 2), labeled N.
